$Comment: The standalone RpgStations Cooking Fire work station block (scope-2 wave-3 leg W3-F, design section 2.7 fish exemplar, the remote-anchor half of the cutting-board/cooking-fire pair - it is BOTH a standalone direct cook loop AND the multi-station anchor CuttingBoard/PrepFish claims by proximity+type). Model/texture/hitbox lifted from the vanilla Deco_Campfire_Off (ledger [6cdea5ead]) - the diegetic F-loop deliberately keeps its OWN rpg_station_use RootInteraction on Interactions.Use rather than the vanilla Bench_Campfire's auto-open 'Open_Processing_Bench' (the same RPG_Station_Sawmill-vs-Bench_Lumbermill discipline: reuse the model, not the competing Use wiring). THREE states, one per custody phase (Server/RpgStations/Stations/CookingFire.json's Custody.States = {Empty:'Default', Loaded:'Loaded', Working:'Lit'}): Default = the unlit Campfire_Off model/texture with the empty hint; Loaded = the SAME unlit look with the loaded hint (raw fish is sitting on a COLD fire - the Custody.Display prop is the has-fish signal, the block itself must not burn); Lit = the actively-cooking look, held ONLY while a cook/convert step is genuinely running (maintainer ruling 'Lit = actively cooking', engine side StationService#enterWorkingState). The Lit field set is copied VERBATIM off vanilla Furniture_Crude_Brazier.json, the one vanilla block using this exact Campfire.blockymodel + Campfire_Texture.png pair: the animated Fire_Burn blockyanim + Looping, Light #ecb (Bench_Campfire's own Processing-state colour), BlockSoundSetId Campfire, the looping crackle AmbientSoundEventId SFX_Campfire_Default_Loop, and the Campfire_New_Cartoon particle system (flames + Fireplace_Sparks_Up embers + heat distortion) at the brazier's own Scale 0.9 / +0.25Y offset, beside the pre-existing Smoke_Black plume which stays. Crackle + embers are therefore 100% NATIVE and need ZERO engine work: BlockType per-state AmbientSoundEventId is LOOPING-validated ('a looping ambient sound event that emits from this block when placed') and per-state Particles run for the state's whole lifetime, both starting and STOPPING automatically on the setBlockInteractionState flip with no stop packet (none exists in the protocol) - the exact mechanism vanilla Bench_Campfire uses for its own Processing state. VariantRotation is authored NESW (a station-block placement convention, deliberately over the vanilla decorative RandomRotation) so the block's own facing composes correctly with Custody.Display's facing-relative Offset. When claimed as a remote anchor by another station's program, this block's OWN action is never invoked (design 2.2) - only its Custody claim and block state matter there. SELECTION WAVE (decision 51a): the block ALSO carries a native BlockType.Bench{Type:Processing,Id:Campfire} + BlockType.BlockEntity.Components{BenchBlock,ProcessingBenchBlock} (ledger 'Can a mod reuse the native Bench crafting/processing WINDOW' entry, verbatim shape) purely so the engine's sneak+F handler can open the NATIVE processing window (Java-driven PageManager#setPageWithWindows, never an Interactions.Use auto-open) scoped to Bench.Id 'Campfire' - CraftingRecipe.BenchRequirement.Id is a bare open string match, so this reuses the vanilla Food_Fish_Raw -> Food_Fish_Grilled recipe (ledger [6cdea5ead], BenchRequirement:[{Id:'Campfire',Type:'Processing'}]) with ZERO recipe duplication. Bench.Fuel is deliberately OMITTED (ProcessingBenchBlock#tick treats a null Fuel array as fuel-less/always-active per source, ledger-verified) so the native window cooks the fish with no separate fuel item required; Input carries one FilterValidIngredients slot (the vanilla Campfire's own Input-slot shape) so the window has somewhere to receive the raw fish. Plain F still drives the diegetic custody/Lit loop above; sneak+F is the alternate, purely native, instant-crafting door onto the SAME recipe truth (decision 50/51, both routes coexist on one block).
